note: TESTREG's Unika summary names two candidate variables (101 and 102) and an edition both carry, so it binds to neither and raises ambiguous_support_target naming the Unika record itself, which is not one of register 1's original delivery rows. A guarded [[acknowledge]] pins that record (expected_evidence_sha256 over the Unika row selected by its semantic key). From the old test: the unchanged guarded entry settles the issue (acknowledged == {'ambiguous_support_target': 1}) and the scope's variables are as without the entry; here the ambiguous summary supplies no flags, so value and value-2 are withheld (unresolved_flag) and no variable is built either way. From the source-diagnostic test: the entry acknowledges only its own register's issue, so register 2's identical-looking summary issue stays an error.
